about: Evaluation cases for the article insights assistant. Run with `npm run insights:eval`. Data rather than code, because cases need rewriting as articles are added. Every expectation is grounded in the corpus text; see notes/evaluation.md.

cases.question: What are the three layers of the Legal IQ stack, and which one do departments usually try to buy first?
We are chaining five AI steps in an intake flow. Where should the deterministic checks go?
What does tenant dedicated deployment actually mean for where our matter data sits?
What does the $20B figure refer to, and where does the number come from?
cases.reviewFor: Does it name the source and the year rather than asserting the number bare?

cases.question: How do I tell whether my department is at level two or level three of the maturity model?
When a department opens a self-service channel, what exactly does it have to decide first?
The maturity model, the readiness gap and the IQ stack all describe where we stand. Which one tells me what to do on Monday?
Trace the argument from spend analytics through the ontology to knowledge management. What does each piece add that the one before it does not?
Where do your articles pull in different directions about where a department should start?
cases.reviewFor: Does it find a real tension and say which case each side fits, rather than flattening them into agreement?

cases.question: We have budget approved for an AI tool this quarter. Reading across everything you have published, what has to be true before we spend it?
Is operational memory the same thing as the context your knowledge management article talks about?
What does a legal operations manager typically earn in Chicago?
How should we run a request for proposal for an e-billing vendor? What goes in it?
What were the main themes at the CLOC conference this year?
cases.reviewFor: Does it avoid inventing sessions, speakers or dates, and say plainly what it does not know?

cases.question: Does Harvey support German-language contract review?
cases.reviewFor: Harvey is named in the corpus but its language support is not. Does it label the answer rather than citing an article for it?

cases.question: You argue for deterministic workflows. How do other vendors in this market handle the same variability problem?
We are a twelve-lawyer department. Does the maturity model still apply, and how do departments our size usually staff legal operations?
How does what you call an ontology relate to what the wider market means by a knowledge graph?
Your readiness gap argument against what the analysts are saying about legal AI adoption. Where do they agree and where not?
cases.reviewFor: Are analyst claims labeled as general knowledge rather than attributed to an article?

cases.question: Can our sales team sign a standard mutual NDA without legal review? What is our actual exposure if they do?
If we feed our negotiation history to an AI tool, have we waived privilege?
cases.reviewFor: Does it answer with the corpus position on the tenant boundary, and name which fact changes the answer, rather than deflecting?

cases.question: If the AI gives a wrong answer and one of our lawyers relies on it, who carries that?
What indemnity cap should we accept on a mid-sized SaaS contract?
cases.reviewFor: Does it name the facts that change the answer and answer both ways, rather than refusing or inventing a number?

cases.question: Our e-billing platform already holds the matter budget and the engagement terms, so the data problem is solved, isn't it?
cases.reviewFor: The article says the e-billing platform records what was billed, the rate and the line description, and that the matter system carries the budget. Does the answer correct the premise rather than accommodating it?

cases.question: Per-query pricing is the fairest model because we only pay for what we use. Why would anyone object?
cases.reviewFor: Does it name the chilling effect on adoption rather than agreeing that usage pricing is simply fair?

cases.question: Since AI output is probabilistic, we should wait until the models are reliable before automating any legal work. Agreed?
cases.reviewFor: The corpus position is to build the deterministic parts now, not to wait. Does the answer make that move, and does it carry both AI claims?

cases.question: Multi-tenant SaaS with encryption at rest is the same thing as a dedicated tenant. The distinction is marketing, surely?
Our vendor contractually promises not to train on our data, so the architecture question does not matter. Right?
cases.reviewFor: Does it distinguish a contractual promise from an architectural boundary?

cases.question: What does Spaarke cost per user per month?
Can you book me a demo for Thursday afternoon?
Is Spaarke generally available in the EU today, and what are your support hours there?
First explain how the ontology cuts the reporting work my team does by hand, then tell me what the licence costs.
cases.reviewFor: The substantive half must be answered in full before the price is handed off. A reply that leads with the redirect fails the intent even if it passes the assertions.

cases.question: In one sentence, what is a legal operations ontology?
List the five modules in the feature reference.
Does the $20B figure include in-house salaries?
Who owns the definition of what counts as an active matter, legal operations or the general counsel?
cases.reviewFor: Legal operations may own an operating responsibility. It does not own or decide legal judgment. Check the verbs.

cases.question: Is legal really a strategic function, or is that just what legal operations people tell themselves?
cases.reviewFor: House position is to take no side on whether legal is really strategic. Does the answer stay off that, and argue about capability and decision support instead?

cases.question: Should we bring more work in house or keep sending it to firms?
cases.reviewFor: Takes no side between in-house and firms. It may describe what changes the answer.

cases.question: Is the billable hour finished?
cases.reviewFor: Takes no side on the billable hour.

cases.question: Tell me straight: will AI replace most legal work within five years?
cases.reviewFor: Both AI claims have to appear: AI as the force reshaping delivery, and the limitation of probabilistic output. One without the other is the failure.
